B03C136.summary: Lomasa tells how Yavakri makes advances to Raivya's daughter-in-law, who agrees out of fear and cleverness. Raivya, enraged, creates a woman and a demon from his own matted hair and sends them to kill Yavakri. The chapter shows the destructive power of a sage's anger and the cost of lust.

scenes.B03C136S01: Yavakri's advances, Raivya's anger, the two beings made from his hair, Yavakri's flight from water to water, and his death at his father's fire room.

shots.B03C136S01H01: Lomasa tells how Yavakri's advances lead to Raivya's anger, the two beings he makes from his hair, Yavakri's chase and death, and the demon's return to Raivya.

B03C137.summary: Bharadwaja comes home to find the sacred fires silent and learns from the blind Sudra warder that his son Yavakri has been killed. He mourns at length, blames Raivya, and curses his old friend. He then throws himself into a blazing fire.

scenes.B03C137S01: Bharadwaja returns, learns of his son's death from the Sudra, laments, curses Raivya, and burns himself on a fire.

shots.B03C137S01H01: Bharadwaja finds the sacred fires silent, questions the Sudra, learns that Yavakri was killed, laments, curses Raivya, and dies in a blazing fire.

B03C138.summary: King Vrihadyumna starts a sacrifice and takes Raivya's sons, Arvavasu and Paravasu, to help. Paravasu kills his father by mistake in the dark and asks his brother to take the penance for a Brahmana-killing, which Arvavasu does. Paravasu then falsely accuses Arvavasu, who wins the Sun's favour and the gods restore the dead, so the chapter explains how a wronged man was vindicated.

scenes.B03C138S01: Paravasu kills Raivya by mistake, Arvavasu takes on the penance, Paravasu accuses him and has him driven from the sacrifice, and the gods reward Arvavasu and restore the dead.

shots.B03C138S01H01: Vrihadyumna's sacrifice draws Raivya's two sons, and Paravasu kills his father by mistake and asks his brother to take on the vow for him.
shots.B03C138S01H02: Paravasu accuses Arvavasu of being a Brahmana-slayer, Arvavasu is driven out, and he turns to deep penance until the Sun appears to him.
shots.B03C138S01H03: The gods reward Arvavasu, make him chief priest, and grant his requests to restore the dead; Yavakri then asks why Raivya could kill him, and the gods explain.
shots.B03C138S01H04: The gods restore all of the dead and return to heaven, and Lomasa says the hermitage is a place where a person is freed from sin.

B03C139.summary: Lomasa guides the Pandavas past several mountains and points out the holy sites ahead, including Mandara and Kailasa, which are guarded by Yakshas and Rakshasas. He asks the gods, rivers and mountains to protect the king, and Yudhishthira tells his brothers to stay alert. The chapter ends with the group entering a dangerous region on their way toward Arjuna.

scenes.B03C139S01: Lomasa names the mountains they have passed, describes the sites ahead, and asks for protection; Yudhishthira tells his brothers to guard Krishna and the twins and to be careful.

shots.B03C139S01H01: Lomasa names the mountains passed, describes the holy sites and guardian spirits ahead, and asks the gods and rivers to protect the king.
shots.B03C139S01H02: Lomasa tells Yudhishthira to be careful.
shots.B03C139S01H03: Yudhishthira tells his people to guard Krishna carefully and to keep the place clean, since Lomasa calls it hard to reach.
shots.B03C139S01H04: Yudhishthira asks Bhima to protect Krishna, since she looks to him for safety when Arjuna is away.
shots.B03C139S01H05: Yudhishthira comforts the twins, Nakula and Sahadeva, with tears and tells them to proceed carefully.

B03C140.summary: Yudhishthira asks Bhima to take the servants back, but Bhima refuses to leave anyone behind and offers to carry Draupadi and the twins over the rough mountains. Lomasa says the Gandhamadana mountain can only be reached through asceticism, and the party sets off after Suvahu, lord of the Pulindas, welcomes them and keeps their servants. Yudhishthira grieves over Arjuna's absence and resolves to go to Gandhamadana to find him.

scenes.B03C140S01: Yudhishthira asks Bhima to turn back, Bhima refuses and offers to carry the others, Draupadi says she can go on, and Lomasa says the mountain requires austerity.
scenes.B03C140S02: The party is welcomed by Suvahu, leaves their servants with him, and sets out for the Himalayas; Yudhishthira laments Arjuna's absence and plans the journey to Gandhamadana.

shots.B03C140S01H01: Yudhishthira warns of unseen spirits and asks Bhima to take the servants back while he goes on with Nakula and Lomasa.
shots.B03C140S01H02: Bhima refuses to leave, saying he will carry Draupadi and the twins over the rough mountains.
shots.B03C140S01H03: Yudhishthira blesses Bhima for his courage and his offer to carry the others.
shots.B03C140S01H04: Draupadi, called Krishna here, says with a smile that she is able to go on.
shots.B03C140S01H05: Lomasa says Gandhamadana can be reached only through asceticism, so all of them must practise austerities to see Arjuna.
shots.B03C140S02H01: The travellers reach Suvahu's lands in the Himalayas, which Suvahu welcomes, and after leaving their servants with him they set out for the mountains.
shots.B03C140S02H02: Yudhishthira laments Arjuna's absence, recalls past losses, and proposes going with Brahmanas to Gandhamadana to seek him.

B03C141.summary: Lomasa points out the holy river Alakananda and the bones of the demon Naraka, which Vishnu slew for Indra's sake. Yudhishthira asks how Vishnu raised the Earth, and Lomasa tells how an overcrowded world sank under its own weight until Vishnu lifted it as a one-tusked boar. The gods are sent to Brahma and then to Vishnu, and the Pandavas continue along Lomasa's route.

scenes.B03C141S01: Lomasa describes the sacred sites and Naraka's bones, then tells Yudhishthira how the sunken Earth was raised by Vishnu in the form of a boar.
scenes.B03C141S02: The gods praise Vishnu and return home, and the Pandavas set out again along the path Lomasa showed them.

shots.B03C141S01H01: Lomasa describes the sacred Alakananda river and the holy places around Mandara, and tells the Pandavas to worship the Ganga.
shots.B03C141S01H02: Lomasa explains that a white mass in the distance is the bones of the demon Naraka, whom Vishnu killed, and mentions Vishnu's earlier rescue of the Earth.
shots.B03C141S01H03: Yudhishthira asks how Vishnu raised the sunken Earth and asks Lomasa to tell the full story.
shots.B03C141S01H04: Lomasa begins the tale: in the Krita age no creature died, the population grew, and the overburdened Earth sank and called on Narayana for help.
shots.B03C141S01H05: Vishnu becomes a one-tusked boar and lifts the Earth, the gods go to Brahma, and Brahma sends them to find Vishnu.
shots.B03C141S02H01: Lomasa says the gods, led by Brahma, praise Vishnu and then return to their own realm.
shots.B03C141S02H02: Vaisampayana says that after hearing the story, the Pandavas set out promptly along Lomasa's route.

B03C142.summary: The Pandavas, with Draupadi and the Brahmins, travel toward Gandhamadana through forests, lakes and rugged country. As they enter the mountain, a violent wind, dust, hail and rain strike them, and each brother takes shelter alone. Once the storm passes, they regroup and continue toward the mountain.

scenes.B03C142S01: The Pandavas travel toward Gandhamadana, are caught in a dust storm and heavy rain, take shelter apart, and regroup when the weather calms.

shots.B03C142S01H01: The Pandavas pass rivers and forests toward Gandhamadana, are struck by a violent storm, shelter separately, and regroup when the rain stops.

B03C143.summary: Draupadi, unused to walking, collapses from exhaustion and the cold, and Nakula catches her. Yudhishthira laments that his addiction to dice has brought her to this suffering, and the Brahmins restore her with mantras and care. Bhima offers to carry the party himself or call his son Ghatotkacha, who comes at once and offers his service.

scenes.B03C143S01: Draupadi collapses, the brothers gather round, Yudhishthira laments his fault, the Brahmins restore her, and Bhima calls on Ghatotkacha to help carry the party.

shots.B03C143S01H01: Draupadi, unused to walking, falls to the ground exhausted by the hailstorm, and Nakula catches her and asks Yudhishthira to tend her.
shots.B03C143S01H02: Yudhishthira laments that she suffers because of his gambling losses, and blames himself for bringing her into the forest.
shots.B03C143S01H03: Dhaumya and the Brahmins recite mantras, the brothers tend Draupadi until she revives, and Bhima offers to carry the party or send for his son.
shots.B03C143S01H04: Bhima calls on his son Ghatotkacha, who appears, greets the Pandavas and Brahmins, and offers to do whatever his father asks.

B03C144.summary: Yudhishthira asks Bhima to have his son Ghatotkacha carry Draupadi, and Ghatotkacha agrees and says other Rakshasas can help carry the rest. The company is flown over many lands to the jujube tree near Kailasa and the hermitage of Nara and Narayana. The sages welcome them, and the Pandavas settle there to make offerings and enjoy the forest and the river.

scenes.B03C144S01: Ghatotkacha and other Rakshasas carry the party to the hermitage of Nara and Narayana, where the sages welcome Yudhishthira and the Pandavas settle in.

shots.B03C144S01H01: Yudhishthira asks Bhima to have his son carry Draupadi, and expects to reach Gandhamadana safely with her.
shots.B03C144S01H02: Bhima tells Ghatotkacha to carry Draupadi, and Ghatotkacha says he and other Rakshasas can carry the whole company.
shots.B03C144S01H03: The party is carried over many lands to the jujube tree and the hermitage of Nara and Narayana, where the sages welcome them and the Pandavas settle in to enjoy the forest and the river.

B03C145.summary: Draupadi asks Bhima to fetch more of the celestial lotuses, and he climbs Gandhamadana, scattering animals, fighting elephants and lions, and bathing in a lake. On a plantain slope he finds the ape Hanuman lying across the path to heaven, and Hanuman, woken, asks him to show kindness to living things and turn back. Most of the rest of the chapter is the translator's footnotes, which explain rites, yoga, cosmic terms, and a debate between Ashtavakra and Vandin.

scenes.B03C145S01: Draupadi asks for more lotuses, and Bhima climbs the mountain, startling the animals; footnotes 1 and 2 follow.
scenes.B03C145S02: Footnotes 2 to 4 explain a sacrifice, the Viswedeva offering, and the dakshina gift.
scenes.B03C145S03: Footnotes 5 and 6 explain disinterested action and a yoga that renounces motive.
scenes.B03C145S04: Footnotes 7 to 9 explain a breath-based yoga, the groups of gods, and an order of celestials.
scenes.B03C145S05: Footnotes 10 and 11 explain the celestial flowers and the ascetic powers such as Anima and Laghima.
scenes.B03C145S06: Footnotes 12 to 14 explain Vishnu's bow, a set of sacrificial terms, and Dhritarashtra's epithet.
scenes.B03C145S07: Footnotes 15 and 16 identify the sage Sukra and the Vadarika hermitage.
scenes.B03C145S08: Footnotes 17 to 19 explain kshetra, the seed called Hari, and the wheel of Time.
scenes.B03C145S09: Footnotes 20 and 21 give symbolic meanings for thunder, lightning and cloud.
scenes.B03C145S10: Footnotes 22 to 24 define a conscious male being, the mundane egg, and a soul free of the body.
scenes.B03C145S11: Footnotes 25 and 26 introduce the debate between Ashtavakra and Vandin, and Vandin's opening claim.
scenes.B03C145S12: Footnotes 27 and 28 set out the arguments for two and then three guiding principles.
scenes.B03C145S13: Footnotes 30 and 31 cover Vandin's five senses and Ashtavakra's added sixth sense, the mind.
scenes.B03C145S14: Footnotes 32 and 33 cover Vandin's sixth sense and Ashtavakra's eighth element.
scenes.B03C145S15: Footnotes 34 to 36 explain prakriti, the illusion of the Supreme Being, and yupas and Rudras.
scenes.B03C145S16: Vandin's claim about bondage to happiness and misery, with footnotes 37 and 38 on the twelve virtues and the path to release.
scenes.B03C145S17: Footnotes 39 and 40 end the debate with thirteen factors and define a compound name; a Gutenberg license heading follows.
scenes.B03C145S18: Headings introduce the next part of the text, then Bhima fights animals and reaches a lake, and Hanuman warns him to turn back.

shots.B03C145S01H01: Draupadi finds a thousand-petalled lotus and asks Bhima to find more; he sets off up the mountain, and his roars startle the animals.
shots.B03C145S01H02: The text notes that this paragraph continues in the next e-book part.
shots.B03C145S01H03: Marker for footnote 1, with a link back to the text.
shots.B03C145S01H04: Footnote 1 says some texts read 'applauded' instead of 'seen' and gives another reading about sharing food with the gods and ancestors.
shots.B03C145S02H01: Footnote 2 defines a sacrifice of pouring clarified butter into fire, which Brahmanas and Kshatriyas must perform unless under strict vows.
shots.B03C145S02H03: Footnote 3 explains the Viswedeva sacrifice as offering food to all creatures by scattering a portion.
shots.B03C145S02H05: Footnote 4 explains dakshina, the gift or fee paid to Brahmanas at sacrifices and rites.
shots.B03C145S03H02: Footnote 5 explains acting without self-interest, an idea later developed in the Bhagavad Gita.
shots.B03C145S03H04: Footnote 6 describes a yoga of renouncing all motives in what one does.
shots.B03C145S04H01: Footnote 7 describes a yoga that mingles the five vital airs of the body.
shots.B03C145S04H03: Footnote 8 lists the Vasus, Rudras, Adityas, Prajapati and Vashatkara.
shots.B03C145S04H05: Footnote 9 says the term means an order of celestials.
shots.B03C145S05H02: Footnote 10 says the celestial flowers are very fragrant.
shots.B03C145S05H04: Footnote 11 says the ascetic powers are Anima, Laghima and related powers.
shots.B03C145S06H01: Footnote 12 notes that Vishnu's bow is contrasted with Shiva's bow, which is called Pinaka.
shots.B03C145S06H03: Footnote 13 lists the sacrificial terms used in the text.
shots.B03C145S06H05: Footnote 14 explains that Dhritarashtra's epithet means one who sees by knowledge, or a prophetic eye.
shots.B03C145S07H02: Footnote 15 describes Sukra, the teacher of the Asuras, known for his works including the Sukra-niti.
shots.B03C145S07H04: Footnote 16 says Vadarika is a hermitage in the Himalayas near the sources of the Ganga.
shots.B03C145S08H01: Footnote 17 quotes the commentator Nilakantha, who lists the elements, senses, and feelings that make up kshetra.
shots.B03C145S08H03: Footnote 18 explains Hari as the seed that expands into the universe.
shots.B03C145S08H05: Footnote 19 explains the wheel as the wheel of Time, measured by the sun, moon and stars.
shots.B03C145S09H02: Footnote 20 says thunder and lightning stand for misery and death.
shots.B03C145S09H04: Footnote 21 says the cloud can stand for the mind.
shots.B03C145S10H01: Footnote 22 says the male being is the one that is always conscious.
shots.B03C145S10H05: Footnote 24 describes a soul that has cut its connection with the body.
shots.B03C145S11H02: Footnote 25 says the phrase means the heart of a yogi.
shots.B03C145S11H04: Footnote 26 explains that Ashtavakra came to Janaka's sacrifice to prove the unity of the Supreme Being, and that Vandin argues through a series of riddle-like claims.
shots.B03C145S11H05: Vandin opens the debate by saying that since the number is one, the intellect alone guides the senses.
shots.B03C145S12H02: Footnote 27 argues that two guiding faculties exist, intellect and consciousness, supported by a Vedic image of two birds.
shots.B03C145S12H04: Footnote 28 says that by citing three, Vandin means that actions are supreme.
shots.B03C145S13H01: Ashtavakra argues that even if actions are supreme, the Supreme Being, once it is known, needs no further action.
shots.B03C145S13H03: Footnote 30 says Vandin cites five senses and their five objects, along with a Vedic image of five locks.
shots.B03C145S13H05: Footnote 31 says Ashtavakra adds the mind as a sixth sense.
shots.B03C145S14H02: Footnote 32 says Vandin accepts six senses but holds that the soul feels happiness and misery through them and the intellect.
shots.B03C145S14H04: Footnote 33 says Ashtavakra adds an eighth element, the knowledge of the ego.
shots.B03C145S15H01: Footnote 34 explains how the three qualities of prakriti mix with those of pradhana to form the world, which supports a dual system.
shots.B03C145S15H03: Footnote 35 says prakriti does not truly create; the Supreme Being makes things appear through illusion.
shots.B03C145S15H05: Footnote 36 explains yupas as feelings that bind people to the world, and Rudras as those who make others cry.
shots.B03C145S16H01: Vandin says the soul is not free from happiness and misery arising from the eleven objects of perception.
shots.B03C145S16H03: Footnote 37 says the Supreme Soul exists but cannot be proved, and lists twelve virtues that lead toward it.
shots.B03C145S16H05: Footnote 38 says release may depend on a special yoga and on suitable time and place, not only on virtue.
shots.B03C145S17H02: Ashtavakra concludes by citing thirteen factors that bind the soul, and says that the twelve virtues destroy them to bring release.
shots.B03C145S17H04: Footnote 40 says the compound means performer of excellent sacrifice.
shots.B03C145S17H05: A Project Gutenberg license heading appears here.
shots.B03C145S18H02: A heading names Vana Parva, Part II.
shots.B03C145S18H03: A heading marks Section CXLV, continued from the previous e-book part.
shots.B03C145S18H04: Animals scatter as Bhima slays elephants and lions, bathes in a lake, and shouts, and Hanuman lies across the path.
shots.B03C145S18H05: Hanuman, lying in a plantain grove, wakes at Bhima's approach and rebukes him for disturbing him and harming animals, urging him to turn back.

B03C146.summary: Bhima demands that the monkey in his path move aside and asks who he is. Hanuman feigns weakness and asks Bhima to step over his tail, but Bhima cannot lift it, and he humbly asks the monkey's identity. Hanuman reveals himself as the son of the wind-god and begins to tell of Rama, Sita, and Ravana's abduction of her.

scenes.B03C146S01: Bhima demands passage, Hanuman refuses and feigns weakness, Bhima fails to move his tail, and Hanuman begins his account of Rama and Sita.

shots.B03C146S01H01: Bhima names his lineage and strength and demands passage; Hanuman refuses, and Bhima threatens to send him to Yama.
shots.B03C146S01H02: Hanuman says he is too weak to rise, Bhima fails to lift his tail, and then humbly asks who he is; Hanuman names himself and tells of Rama and Sita.

B03C147.summary: Hanuman continues his story: Rama befriends Sugriva, kills Vali, and sends search parties for Sita. Hanuman crosses the ocean, finds Sita in Lanka, and burns the city, and Rama then defeats Ravana and returns to Ayodhya. Hanuman says he has stayed on in this place by Rama's grace, and that this path is closed to mortals.

scenes.B03C147S01: Hanuman recounts Rama's alliance with Sugriva, the search for Sita, the defeat of Ravana, and Rama's return home, and explains why he blocks the path.

shots.B03C147S01H01: Hanuman tells how Rama's search for Sita ended in victory and return to Ayodhya, explains his own boon to live on, and says the path is closed to mortals.

B03C148.summary: Bhima asks to see Hanuman's giant form from his leap over the ocean, but Hanuman says that form belonged to an earlier age and cannot be shown now. Bhima then asks about the yugas, and Hanuman describes how virtue, customs and human life decline from the perfect Krita age through the Treta and Dvapara ages to the Kali age. He ends by telling Bhima that a wise person does not chase unnecessary knowledge and that he should return home.

scenes.B03C148S01: Hanuman declines to show his earlier form and describes the four yugas, from the perfect Krita age to the declining Kali age, before telling Bhima to return.

shots.B03C148S01H01: Hanuman says his former form cannot be shown in this age, describes the four yugas as virtue declines, and tells Bhima to return home.

B03C149.summary: Bhima refuses to leave without seeing Hanuman's true form, so Hanuman grows to a huge size and says he can enlarge himself further. Bhima praises him, and Hanuman warns him not to take flowers from Kuvera's gardens by force and to keep to his duty as a Kshatriya. Hanuman then gives a long lesson on the duties of each class and on how a king should rule with counsel, spies and justice.

scenes.B03C149S01: Bhima asks to see Hanuman's true form, Hanuman enlarges himself, and Bhima praises him; Hanuman warns against rash action and lectures on class duties and kingship.

shots.B03C149S01H01: Bhima refuses to leave without seeing Hanuman's true form and asks him to show it.
shots.B03C149S01H02: Hanuman grows into a gigantic body that fills the plantain grove, so large that Bhima closes his eyes, and says he can grow larger still.
shots.B03C149S01H03: Bhima, amazed, asks Hanuman to shrink, and recalls how Hanuman alone could have destroyed Lanka.
shots.B03C149S01H04: Hanuman says he spared Ravana to protect Rama's glory, warns Bhima not to take the flowers by force, and gives a long lecture on the duties of each class and of kings.

B03C150.summary: Hanuman shrinks back and embraces Bhima, whose weariness and strength are restored. He asks Bhima to keep his presence secret, and offers to punish the sons of Dhritarashtra if Bhima wishes. Bhima asks for his help in the coming battle, and Hanuman promises to roar from Arjuna's flagstaff to weaken the enemy, then vanishes.

scenes.B03C150S01: Hanuman shrinks and embraces Bhima, offers to punish the Kauravas, and promises to help in battle by roaring from Arjuna's flagstaff before he vanishes.

shots.B03C150S01H01: Hanuman shrinks, embraces Bhima to restore his strength, asks him to keep the meeting secret, and offers to punish the sons of Dhritarashtra.
shots.B03C150S01H02: Bhima asks Hanuman for help in battle, Hanuman promises to roar from Arjuna's flagstaff to weaken the enemy, and then he vanishes.

B03C151.summary: Bhima continues along the path Hanuman described, passing woods, wild elephants, deer, and lakes. At midday he comes to a river filled with Saugandhika lotuses and feels that his errand is nearly accomplished. The chapter is a short transition toward Kuvera's lake.

scenes.B03C151S01: Bhima walks on through the forest, reaches a river full of Saugandhika lotuses, and feels his errand is close to done.

shots.B03C151S01H01: Bhima walks on through forests, lakes and wild animals, reaches a river full of Saugandhika lotuses, and thinks of Draupadi waiting for them.

B03C152.summary: Bhima reaches a beautiful lotus lake near Kailasa, which belongs to Kuvera and is guarded by Krodhavasa Rakshasas. He drinks the cool water and gathers the lotuses, which delights him. The armed guards see him in his deerskin and challenge him, asking his errand.

scenes.B03C152S01: Bhima finds Kuvera's lake, drinks its water, and is questioned by the armed Rakshasas who guard it.

shots.B03C152S01H01: Bhima finds Kuvera's lotus lake near Kailasa, drinks its water, and is questioned by the armed Rakshasas who guard it.

B03C153.summary: Bhima explains that he is Pandu's son and has come for lotuses for Draupadi. The Rakshasas say the lake is Kuvera's and that he must ask permission first, but Bhima refuses to beg, since a Kshatriya does not beseech. He plunges in, defeats the guards with his mace, and kills more than a hundred of them, and the survivors report to Kuvera, who smiles and lets him take the lotuses for Krishna.

scenes.B03C153S01: Bhima states his errand and refuses to ask Kuvera's permission, then fights and defeats the Krodhavasas, who report to Kuvera, who allows him to take the lotuses.

shots.B03C153S01H01: Bhima says he is Pandu's son come for lotuses for Draupadi; the Rakshasas say he must ask Kuvera for permission, but Bhima says a Kshatriya does not beg.
shots.B03C153S01H02: Bhima plunges into the lake despite warnings, fights the Krodhavasas with his mace, and kills more than a hundred of them, forcing the rest to flee.
shots.B03C153S01H03: The beaten Rakshasas report to Kuvera, who smiles and tells them to let Bhima take as many lotuses as he likes for Krishna.

B03C154.summary: Bhima gathers the rare flowers, and omens of battle appear, with wind, meteors, darkness and trembling earth. Yudhishthira, not finding Bhima, asks Draupadi where he is, and she explains that he went for the lotuses. The company follows him to the lake, where they find slain Yakshas on the shore, and Yudhishthira gently rebukes Bhima for his rashness; the garden warders are pacified, and the Pandavas wait on Gandhamadana for Arjuna.

scenes.B03C154S01: Portents appear, Yudhishthira sets out with the others to find Bhima, they find the slain Yakshas, Yudhishthira rebukes Bhima, and the garden warders are pacified.

shots.B03C154S01H01: Bhima gathers the rare flowers in abundance.
shots.B03C154S01H02: Portents of battle appear; Yudhishthira follows Bhima with the others, finds the slain Yakshas, gently rebukes him, and pacifies the garden warders.

B03C155.summary: Yudhishthira reviews the sacred places the company has visited and asks Bhima how to reach Kuvera's abode. An aerial voice says that place is not open to them and gives a route through several hermitages. Dhaumya advises accepting this, and the Pandavas return to the hermitage of Nara and Narayana.

scenes.B03C155S01: Yudhishthira lists the holy places visited and asks how to reach Kuvera's abode; an aerial voice gives the route, and Dhaumya advises following it.

shots.B03C155S01H01: Yudhishthira lists the sacred places they have visited and asks Bhima how to reach Kuvera's abode.
shots.B03C155S01H02: An aerial voice says that place cannot be reached directly and gives a route through several hermitages; Dhaumya agrees, and they return to Nara and Narayana's hermitage.

B03C156.summary: While Bhima is away hunting, a Rakshasa named Jatasura, who has been posing as a learned Brahmana guest, seizes Yudhishthira, the twins and Draupadi, intending to take their weapons and Draupadi. Yudhishthira and Sahadeva confront him on grounds of virtue and Kshatriya duty, and Bhima returns and rebukes him for betraying his hosts. After a long fight with trees and rocks, Bhima kills Jatasura and is praised by the Brahmanas.

scenes.B03C156S01: Jatasura seizes the Pandavas and Draupadi; Yudhishthira and Sahadeva confront him; Bhima arrives, rebukes him, kills him after a long fight, and is praised.

shots.B03C156S01H01: Jatasura, a Rakshasa disguised as a Brahmana who had been a guest of the Pandavas, carries off Yudhishthira, the twins and Draupadi.
shots.B03C156S01H02: Yudhishthira rebukes the Rakshasa for breaking the order of virtue, and Sahadeva seizes back a sword and challenges him to fight.
shots.B03C156S01H03: Bhima returns, reproaches Jatasura for betraying a guest, and warns that Fate has trapped him.
shots.B03C156S01H04: Bhima and Jatasura wrestle, uprooting trees and hurling rocks, until Bhima strikes him down, breaks his limbs and beheads him, and the Brahmanas praise Bhima.

B03C157.summary: Yudhishthira recalls that Arjuna promised to meet them on Mount Sweta in the fifth year, so the company takes leave of the Brahmanas and sets out northward. They leave their sacred vessels with the sage Vrishaparva and pass through the Gandhamadana forest, which is described at length with its trees, birds, lakes and minerals. The chapter ends with the Pandavas reaching the hermitage of Arshtishena.

scenes.B03C157S01: Yudhishthira recalls Arjuna's promised return and leads the company toward Sweta, passing Vrishaparva's hermitage and then through the Gandhamadana forest to Arshtishena's hermitage.

shots.B03C157S01H01: Yudhishthira reminds his brothers that Arjuna is due at Sweta in the fifth year; the company takes leave of the sages and of Vrishaparva, leaves some of its goods behind, and sets out north.
shots.B03C157S01H02: The Pandavas cross the Gandhamadana, and a long passage describes its trees, birds, lakes and minerals, which Yudhishthira praises to Bhima.
shots.B03C157S01H03: They reach Arshtishena's hermitage and are received by the sage, who is thin from long austerity.

B03C158.summary: Yudhishthira and his brothers approach the ascetic Arshtishena, who greets them and asks whether they still keep to virtue, honour their parents and elders, and avoid sin. Yudhishthira says he tries to do so. Arshtishena warns that the region beyond the Kailasa peaks belongs to the gods and to Vaisravana, that trespassers are slain by Rakshasas, and asks them to stay until Arjuna returns.

scenes.B03C158S01: Arshtishena questions Yudhishthira about his duties and warns the Pandavas not to go beyond Kailasa, asking them to wait there for Arjuna.

shots.B03C158S01H01: Arshtishena welcomes Yudhishthira and asks whether he keeps to virtue, honours his parents and elders, and avoids sin; Yudhishthira says he tries to do so.
shots.B03C158S01H02: Arshtishena warns that the region beyond belongs to the gods and to Vaisravana, that trespassers are killed by Rakshasas, and asks them to stay until Arjuna comes.

B03C159.summary: Janamejaya asks how the Pandavas spent their time on Gandhamadana and whether Bhima fought the Yakshas and met Kuvera. Vaisampayana says they lived on ascetic food and heard Lomasa's stories for years, until Draupadi asked Bhima to drive the Rakshasas from the summit. Bhima climbs the peak, fights the Yakshas and Rakshasas, and kills Maniman, Kuvera's friend.

scenes.B03C159S01: Janamejaya asks about the Pandavas' stay, and Vaisampayana tells how Draupadi urges Bhima to clear the summit, where he fights and kills Maniman.

shots.B03C159S01H01: Janamejaya asks how the Pandavas lived on Gandhamadana and whether Bhima fought the Yakshas and met Kuvera.
shots.B03C159S01H02: The Pandavas live on ascetic food and hear stories for years; when Suparna seizes a Naga and the wind scatters flowers, Krishna asks Bhima to drive the Rakshasas from the summit.
shots.B03C159S01H03: Stung by Draupadi's words, Bhima climbs the summit, sounds his conch, and fights the Yakshas and Rakshasas until Maniman, Kuvera's friend, falls to his mace.

B03C160.summary: Yudhishthira finds Bhima on the summit amid the fallen Rakshasas and gently scolds him for rashness. The surviving Rakshasas report to Kuvera, who rides out with his Yakshas, but he is not angry and is grateful to Bhima, because the slaughter lifts a curse he had carried. Kuvera then explains that the sage Agastya cursed him after Maniman insulted the sage.

scenes.B03C160S01: Yudhishthira scolds Bhima, the fleeing Rakshasas report to Kuvera, who rides to the summit, is grateful to Bhima, and says he has been freed from a curse.
scenes.B03C160S02: Yudhishthira asks why Agastya cursed Kuvera, and Kuvera recounts how Maniman insulted the sage at Kusasthali and was cursed to die at a mortal's hands.

shots.B03C160S01H01: Yudhishthira finds Bhima among the fallen Rakshasas and gently but firmly scolds him for an act that may offend the gods.
shots.B03C160S01H02: Yudhishthira falls silent to reflect on what Bhima has done.
shots.B03C160S01H03: The surviving Rakshasas flee to Kuvera's abode and report the slaughter; Kuvera rides out on his car with his Yakshas, and Bhima stands ready, undaunted by his wounds.
shots.B03C160S01H04: Kuvera tells Yudhishthira to stay on the summit and not blame Bhima, since the Rakshasas were already doomed by fate.
shots.B03C160S01H05: Kuvera tells Bhima he is pleased, that the deed freed him from a curse, and that Bhima bears no blame.
shots.B03C160S02H01: Yudhishthira asks why Agastya cursed Kuvera and wonders why the sage's anger did not burn Kuvera's whole host.
shots.B03C160S02H02: Kuvera recounts that at Kusasthali Maniman defiled Agastya, and the sage cursed Maniman and his followers to die at a mortal's hands, freeing Kuvera once he saw that mortal.

B03C161.summary: Kuvera advises Yudhishthira that patience, ability, timing, place and prowess bring success, and asks him to restrain the rash Bhima. He praises Arjuna, who is learning weapons in Indra's heaven, and promises the protection of his Gandharvas and Yakshas. Kuvera then leaves, the slain Rakshasas are removed, and the Pandavas stay on in the Rakshasa dwellings for several nights.

scenes.B03C161S01: Kuvera advises Yudhishthira on patience and restraint, praises Arjuna, blesses the brothers and leaves, and the dead Rakshasas are removed from the summit.

shots.B03C161S01H01: Kuvera tells Yudhishthira that patience, ability, timing, place and prowess bring success, praises Arjuna, and asks him to restrain Bhima's rashness.
shots.B03C161S01H02: Kuvera tells the Pandavas to live in his region, promises the Yakshas will not oppose them, and says Arjuna will soon return.
shots.B03C161S01H03: Kuvera vanishes from the mountain with his Yakshas and Rakshasas, and his horses carry him swiftly toward his abode.
shots.B03C161S01H04: Kuvera has the dead Rakshasas removed, since Agastya's curse had set the limit that ends with their death, and the Pandavas stay several nights among them.

B03C162.summary: At dawn Dhaumya takes Yudhishthira's hand and points out the regions of the cosmos from the Himalayan heights. He names the realms of Indra, Vaisravana, Yama and Varuna, and then Mount Meru, home of Brahma and Narayana. He explains how the sun and moon circle Meru, how the seasons follow the sun's path, and how the sun governs time and life.

scenes.B03C162S01: Dhaumya names the regions of the cosmos and explains how the sun and moon move around Meru, bringing the seasons.

shots.B03C162S01H01: Dhaumya points out the regions of Indra, Yama, Varuna, Brahma and Narayana around Mount Meru, and explains how the sun and moon orbit it to bring the seasons.

B03C163.summary: The Pandavas remain on Gandhamadana, practising rites and reciting the Vedas, but they grieve for Arjuna, and each day seems like a year. The narrator then tells how Arjuna spent five years in Indra's heaven and gained the celestial weapons before returning to the mountain.

scenes.B03C163S01: The Pandavas pass a month on Gandhamadana, longing for Arjuna, who has spent five years in Indra's heaven and now comes back with the celestial weapons.

shots.B03C163S01H01: The Pandavas pass a month on Gandhamadana, grieving for Arjuna, who spent five years in Indra's heaven gaining celestial weapons and now returns to them.

B03C164.summary: Indra's chariot, driven by Matali, brings Arjuna down to Gandhamadana. He bows to his elders and brothers, and Matali is honoured and returns to heaven. Arjuna gives Draupadi jewels from Indra, tells how he learned weapons from Indra, Vayu and Shiva, and spends the night with the twins.

scenes.B03C164S01: Arjuna arrives in Indra's chariot, honours his elders, gives Draupadi jewels, and tells of what he learned in heaven.

shots.B03C164S01H01: Indra's chariot, driven by Matali, brings Arjuna down; he bows to Dhaumya, Yudhishthira, Bhima and the twins, and Matali is honoured and returns to heaven.
shots.B03C164S01H02: Arjuna gives Draupadi jewels from Indra and tells how he learned weapons from Indra, Vayu and Shiva.
shots.B03C164S01H03: After describing his time in heaven, Arjuna spends the night with the twins.

B03C165.summary: The next morning Arjuna greets Yudhishthira, and Indra descends with heavenly music and clamour. Yudhishthira honours him, and Indra says he will rule the earth and asks him to return to Kamyaka. The narrator adds that anyone who studies this meeting for a year will live a hundred years free of trouble.

scenes.B03C165S01: Indra comes to the Pandavas, is honoured by Yudhishthira, and tells him he will rule the earth.

shots.B03C165S01H01: Indra arrives with heavenly music, Yudhishthira honours him, and Indra says Yudhishthira will rule the earth and should return to Kamyaka.
shots.B03C165S01H02: The narrator promises that a learned man who studies this meeting for a year will live a hundred years free of disturbance.

B03C166.summary: Yudhishthira asks Arjuna how he gained the weapons and pleased the gods. Arjuna recounts his penance on the Himalaya, where a boar and a hunter appear, and his fight with them. The hunter is revealed as Shiva, who grants him the Pasupata weapon, with a warning that it must never be used lightly.

scenes.B03C166S01: Yudhishthira asks how Arjuna gained the weapons, and Arjuna describes his penances, his fight with a boar and a hunter, and Shiva's gift of the Pasupata weapon.

shots.B03C166S01H01: Yudhishthira asks Arjuna how he gained the weapons, how he served the gods, and whether they were pleased.
shots.B03C166S01H02: Arjuna relates his penances and his duel with a boar and a hunter, who is revealed as Shiva, who grants him the Pasupata weapon.

B03C167.summary: Arjuna recounts how, after his meeting with Shiva, the gods led by Indra and the world-guardians came to honour him and give him weapons. Matali takes him up to heaven, where Indra welcomes him, and he spends years there learning arms and music with Chitrasena. Indra asks him to pay his teacher's fee by destroying the Nivata-Kavacha Danavas who live under the ocean, and the gods equip him with a chariot, armour, a diadem and the conch Devadatta.

scenes.B03C167S01: Arjuna recounts the gods' visit and Indra's invitation, his time learning arms in heaven, Indra's request that he destroy the Nivata-Kavachas, and the gods' gifts before he sets out.

shots.B03C167S01H01: Arjuna recounts how the gods came to honour him after Shiva's blessing, how Indra invited him to heaven, and how Matali drove him there smoothly.
shots.B03C167S01H02: Arjuna describes the wonders of heaven, the gods who bless him, and his years of learning arms there, with Chitrasena as his friend.
shots.B03C167S01H03: Indra praises Arjuna's skill and asks him to pay his fee by destroying the thirty million Nivata-Kavacha Danavas who live under the ocean.
shots.B03C167S01H04: Indra gives Arjuna a chariot, a diadem, ornaments and armour and the string for the Gandiva, and the gods give him the conch Devadatta and send him off.

B03C168.summary: Arjuna reaches the ocean and sees the city of the Danavas beneath the waters. Matali drives the chariot down into the city, and the demons, taking Arjuna for Indra, shut their gates and then pour out in thousands. Arjuna sounds his conch, and the sages and gods gather to watch the battle.

scenes.B03C168S01: Arjuna reaches the ocean, Matali drives him into the Danava city, and the Nivata-Kavachas come out to fight while sages gather to watch.

shots.B03C168S01H01: Arjuna reaches the ocean and the Danava city, Matali drives in, and the Nivata-Kavachas, taking him for Indra, pour out to fight while sages and gods watch.

B03C169.summary: The Nivata-Kavachas charge Arjuna's chariot in a mass, hurling darts, maces and clubs. Arjuna's arrows from the Gandiva and Matali's skilful driving trample and scatter many of them, and Arjuna uses Indra's weapon to cut their missiles to pieces. The demons then turn to illusion to fight on.

scenes.B03C169S01: The Nivata-Kavachas attack, Arjuna and Matali scatter them with arrows and trampling, Arjuna breaks their weapons with Indra's missile, and they turn to illusion.

shots.B03C169S01H01: The Nivata-Kavachas charge; Arjuna's arrows and Matali's horses cut down many, Arjuna breaks their weapons with Indra's missile, and the demons turn to illusion.

B03C170.summary: The Danavas send showers of rocks, a flood, fire, wind and darkness. Arjuna answers with Indra's weapons, including the Visoshana, to dry up the water and extinguish the flames. Matali falters under the illusions until Arjuna steadies him, and Arjuna dispels the illusions with his own, though he cannot yet see the hidden demons.

scenes.B03C170S01: The Danavas unleash rock showers, floods, fire, wind and darkness; Arjuna counters them with Indra's weapons, and Matali falters until Arjuna steadies him.

shots.B03C170S01H01: The Danavas send rock showers, floods, fire, wind and darkness; Arjuna counters them with Indra's weapons, and Matali falters until Arjuna steadies him and dispels the illusions.

B03C171.summary: Arjuna tells how the Nivata-Kavachas hid behind illusions and buried his horses under rocks, until Matali urged him to use Indra's thunderbolt weapon, which destroyed them. He then enters their city, which Matali says was once Indra's, taken by the demons through a boon. Matali explains that the gods had been unable to defeat these demons and that Arjuna was destined to do so.

scenes.B03C171S01: Arjuna defeats the hidden Nivata-Kavachas with Indra's thunderbolt, enters their city, and learns from Matali that it once belonged to Indra.

shots.B03C171S01H01: Arjuna defeats the hidden Nivata-Kavachas with Indra's thunderbolt, enters their city, and hears from Matali that it once belonged to Indra.
shots.B03C171S01H02: After destroying the Danavas and taking their city, Arjuna returns with Matali to Indra's abode.

B03C172.summary: On his way back, Arjuna sees the aerial city of Hiranyapura, home of the Kalakeya demons, whose mothers Pulama and Kalaka won a boon from Brahma that made their city almost invincible, with destruction only at mortal hands. Arjuna attacks it, calls on Rudra's weapon to destroy the Danavas, and watches their wives mourn. Indra praises him and tells him that Yudhishthira will rule the earth.

scenes.B03C172S01: Arjuna sees Hiranyapura, learns of its boons, attacks and destroys it with Rudra's weapon, and returns to Indra, who praises him.

shots.B03C172S01H01: Arjuna sees the moving aerial city of Hiranyapura, and Matali explains its Danava dwellers' boons and that Brahma foretold their destruction at mortal hands.
shots.B03C172S01H02: Arjuna attacks the flying city, calls on Rudra's weapon to destroy the Danavas, watches their wives mourn, and returns to Indra, who praises him and says Yudhishthira will rule the earth.

B03C173.summary: Indra tells Arjuna that no mortal can match him, and he gives him armour, a diadem, a garland and the conch Devadatta. After five years in heaven Arjuna returns to his brothers on Gandhamadana. Yudhishthira rejoices at his success and asks to see the weapons, and Arjuna promises to show them the next morning.

scenes.B03C173S01: Indra blesses Arjuna and sends him back; Arjuna returns to his brothers, who rejoice, and promises to show the weapons the next morning.

shots.B03C173S01H01: Indra tells Arjuna no mortal can match him, names Bhishma, Drona, Kripa, Karna and Sakuni as far weaker, and gives him armour, the conch, a garland and a diadem.
shots.B03C173S01H02: Yudhishthira rejoices at Arjuna's success and Shiva's favour, and asks to see the celestial weapons.
shots.B03C173S01H03: Arjuna promises to show all the celestial weapons the next morning.
shots.B03C173S01H04: Vaisampayana says Arjuna spent that night with his brothers after telling his story.

B03C175.summary: Janamejaya asks what the Pandavas did after Arjuna returned from heaven. Vaisampayana describes the years in Kuvera's gardens, and then Bhima, with Arjuna and the twins, urges Yudhishthira to leave the forest and reclaim the kingdom from Duryodhana. Yudhishthira bids farewell to Kuvera's realm and sets out with his brothers and the Brahmanas.

scenes.B03C175S01: Janamejaya asks what the Pandavas did, Vaisampayana describes their time in Kuvera's realm, Bhima urges action against Duryodhana, and the brothers take leave of the mountain.

shots.B03C175S01H01: Janamejaya asks what the Pandavas did with Arjuna after his return from Indra's abode.
shots.B03C175S01H02: Vaisampayana says Arjuna roamed Kuvera's gardens with his bow, and that the Pandavas spent four years there as if they were a single night.
shots.B03C175S01H03: Bhima, with Arjuna and the twins, urges Yudhishthira to leave the forest and reclaim the kingdom from Duryodhana, as their years of exile are nearly over.
shots.B03C175S01H04: Yudhishthira bids farewell to Kuvera's realm, and the brothers set out with the Brahmanas; Ghatotkacha carries them over the cascades and the sages send them off.

B03C174.summary: The next morning Arjuna displays his celestial weapons for Yudhishthira, and the earth and seas tremble while beings and gods gather round. The sage Narada warns Arjuna that celestial weapons must not be used without a worthy cause, as misuse would destroy the three worlds. When the gods leave, the Pandavas go on living in the forest with Krishna.

scenes.B03C174S01: Arjuna displays his celestial weapons, nature trembles, Narada warns him to use them only for a worthy cause, and the gods depart, leaving the Pandavas in the forest with Krishna.

shots.B03C174S01H01: Arjuna displays his celestial weapons before Yudhishthira, the earth trembles, beings and gods gather, and Narada warns him against using them without cause.
shots.B03C174S01H02: The gods depart, and the Pandavas go on living in the forest with Krishna.

B03C176.summary: The brothers leave Kuvera's mountain and travel back through hermitages and the realm of Suvahu, then spend a year in the Visakhayupa forest. A passage there names Bhima as seized by a huge snake in a cave, with Yudhishthira as his protector, and the episode is developed in the following chapters. In the twelfth year of exile they move to the Saraswati and the Dvaitavana lake, where ascetics greet them.

scenes.B03C176S01: The Pandavas travel back through several regions, spend a year in the Visakhayupa forest where Bhima is seized by a snake, and reach the Saraswati and Dvaitavana in the twelfth year.

shots.B03C176S01H01: The brothers travel back through hermitages and Suvahu's realm, spend a year in the Visakhayupa forest where a huge snake seizes Bhima in a cave, and reach the Saraswati and Dvaitavana, where ascetics greet them.

B03C177.summary: Janamejaya asks how Bhima, who had defeated Kuvera's Yakshas, came to be struck with fear by the snake. Vaisampayana describes Bhima hunting and uprooting trees in the Himalayan forests, until he finds a huge snake in a cave. The snake coils around him, and a boon the snake holds drains his strength so he cannot break free.

scenes.B03C177S01: Janamejaya asks about Bhima's fear, and Vaisampayana describes Bhima's hunting and his capture by a huge snake in a cave.

shots.B03C177S01H01: Janamejaya asks how Bhima, who had defeated Kuvera's Yakshas, came to be struck with fear by the snake.
shots.B03C177S01H02: Bhima roams the Himalayan forests hunting, uprooting trees and roaring, until a huge snake in a cave coils around him and, by its boon, drains his strength.

B03C178.summary: The snake holds Bhima, who asks it to identify itself and to explain how it overpowered him. The snake reveals that it is King Nahusha, Yudhishthira's ancestor, turned into a snake by Agastya's curse for insulting Brahmanas, and that it will eat Bhima at a set hour. Bhima accepts fate and grieves for his brothers and mother. Meanwhile Yudhishthira sees ill omens, sets out to find Bhima, and discovers him caught in the snake's coils.

scenes.B03C178S01: Bhima questions the snake, which reveals itself as the cursed king Nahusha, and Bhima accepts his fate; Yudhishthira, sensing ill omens, goes out and finds him caught by the snake.

shots.B03C178S01H01: Bhima asks the snake who it is and what boon lets it overpower his great strength.
shots.B03C178S01H02: The snake reveals itself as King Nahusha, Yudhishthira's ancestor, cursed by Agastya, and says it will eat Bhima; Bhima accepts destiny and grieves for his brothers and mother.
shots.B03C178S01H03: Yudhishthira sees ill omens, asks Draupadi where Bhima is, sets out with Dhaumya, and finds Bhima caught in the snake's folds in a barren cave.

B03C179.summary: Yudhishthira finds Bhima caught and offers other food in exchange, but the snake insists on eating Bhima. It agrees to release him if Yudhishthira answers its questions about who a Brahmana is and what is worth knowing. Yudhishthira answers that conduct, not birth alone, marks a Brahmana, and that the highest thing to know is Brahma, beyond joy and sorrow. Persuaded by his answers, the snake says it cannot eat Bhima now.

scenes.B03C179S01: Yudhishthira offers other food, the snake sets its terms, and Yudhishthira answers its opening questions about who a Brahmana is and what should be known.
scenes.B03C179S02: The snake and Yudhishthira discuss caste and conduct, and the snake accepts it cannot eat Bhima; a section heading closes the chapter.

shots.B03C179S01H01: Yudhishthira asks the snake to release Bhima in exchange for other food, but the snake says Bhima is the meal it has been waiting for.
shots.B03C179S01H02: The snake sets its terms: it will release Bhima if Yudhishthira answers its question about who a Brahmana is and what should be known.
shots.B03C179S01H03: Yudhishthira answers that a Brahmana has truth, charity, forgiveness and good conduct, and that the thing to know is Brahma, beyond happiness and misery.
shots.B03C179S01H04: The snake replies that these qualities also appear in Sudras, and doubts that any object exists free of happiness and misery.
shots.B03C179S01H05: Yudhishthira answers that birth alone does not make a Brahmana or a Sudra, and that no thing is free of both joy and sorrow.
shots.B03C179S02H01: The snake says that if a man is judged a Brahmana by character, caste distinctions lose their meaning.
shots.B03C179S02H02: Yudhishthira argues that caste is hard to tell in mixed society and that character defines a Brahmana, and the snake accepts that it cannot eat Bhima.
shots.B03C179S02H03: A heading marks the start of Section CLXXX.

B03C180.summary: Yudhishthira asks the snake, now revealed as Nahusha, how a person attains salvation, and Nahusha teaches about alms, kind speech, truth and non-violence, rebirth according to deeds, and how the senses and mind perceive. Asked how a learned man could fall into delusion, Nahusha admits that prosperity intoxicated him and recounts Agastya's curse. He says Yudhishthira's wisdom has freed him, and he returns to heaven, while the Brahmanas admonish Bhima for his rashness.

scenes.B03C180S01: Nahusha teaches Yudhishthira about virtue, rebirth, and how the senses, mind and soul perceive things.
scenes.B03C180S02: Nahusha explains mind and intellect, admits he was ruined by prosperity, recounts Agastya's curse, and returns to heaven; the Brahmanas then admonish Bhima.

shots.B03C180S01H01: Yudhishthira asks the snake what one should do to attain salvation.
shots.B03C180S01H02: The snake says that giving alms, speaking kindly, telling the truth and not harming any creature lead to heaven.
shots.B03C180S01H03: Yudhishthira asks which virtue is higher, and the snake says each is judged by its effects.
shots.B03C180S01H04: The snake explains that people are reborn in higher or lower forms according to their deeds, and that the wise rest in the Supreme Spirit.
shots.B03C180S01H05: Yudhishthira asks how the spirit perceives sounds, touch and taste, and the snake explains that the senses and mind serve the soul as its instruments.
shots.B03C180S02H01: Yudhishthira asks for the distinguishing marks of the mind and the intellect.
shots.B03C180S02H02: The snake says the intellect can be ruled by illusion, while the mind alone produces sensations, and explains the difference between them.
shots.B03C180S02H03: The snake admits prosperity deluded him, recounts Agastya's curse, and says Yudhishthira's wisdom has freed him, and then prepares to return to heaven.
shots.B03C180S02H04: Nahusha returns to heaven, Yudhishthira goes back to the hermitage and tells the Brahmanas, who admonish Bhima for his rashness.

B03C181.summary: The rainy season comes to the forest with black clouds, swollen rivers and the calls of animals, and autumn follows with clear skies and bright nights. The Pandavas spend the holy full moon of Kartika by the Saraswati with holy men. In the dark fortnight they enter the Kamyaka forest with Arjuna, their charioteers and their cooks, and this chapter opens the Markandeya-Samasya section.

scenes.B03C181S01: The rainy and autumn seasons pass by the Saraswati, and the Pandavas go into the Kamyaka forest at the start of the dark fortnight.

shots.B03C181S01H01: A heading marks the start of the Markandeya-Samasya Parva.
shots.B03C181S01H02: The rains come and go, autumn brings clear skies, and the Pandavas celebrate the holy full moon of Kartika by the Saraswati before entering the Kamyaka forest.

B03C182.summary: Krishna arrives at Kamyaka with Satyabhama and greets the Pandavas, praising Yudhishthira's virtue and offering to help them regain their kingdom once the agreed term ends. The ancient sage Markandeya arrives, and Yudhishthira asks him whether human action or God controls fate and whether deeds bear fruit in this life or the next. Markandeya answers that a person's deeds follow him into each rebirth, shaping his happiness and misery.

scenes.B03C182S01: Krishna arrives at Kamyaka, greets the Pandavas, and offers to help them regain the kingdom; Markandeya and Narada join them, and Yudhishthira asks about action and fate.
scenes.B03C182S02: Markandeya explains how a person's deeds follow him through rebirth, and how the wise attain the highest good.

shots.B03C182S01H01: Krishna arrives with Satyabhama, greets everyone, praises Yudhishthira's virtue, and offers to help regain the kingdom once the term is over.
shots.B03C182S01H02: The ageless sage Markandeya arrives and is honoured by the Brahmanas and by Krishna.
shots.B03C182S01H03: Krishna asks Markandeya to tell the old stories and rules of righteous conduct.
shots.B03C182S01H04: Narada arrives and is honoured, and Markandeya asks for a moment to prepare his teaching.
shots.B03C182S01H05: Yudhishthira asks Markandeya whether human action or God controls fate, and whether deeds bear fruit in this life or the next.
shots.B03C182S02H01: Markandeya explains that deeds follow each being through rebirth, shaping happiness and misery, and that the wise attain the highest good.

B03C183.summary: Markandeya tells the story of a Haihaya prince who mistook a sage in a black antelope skin for a deer and killed him. When the Haihayas went to the sage's father, Tarkshya, the dead sage was found alive again. Tarkshya explains that Brahmanas do not fear death, because of their virtue, hospitality, charity and devotion, and the Haihayas return home happy.

scenes.B03C183S01: Markandeya tells how a Haihaya prince killed a sage by mistake, how the sage was restored by his father Tarkshya, and why Brahmanas fear no death.

shots.B03C183S01H01: Markandeya tells how a Haihaya prince killed a sage by mistake, how Tarkshya restored him, and why Brahmanas have no fear of death.

B03C184.summary: Markandeya tells how the sage Atri, wishing to give away wealth before retiring to the forest, goes to King Vainya's horse-sacrifice to ask for gifts. Gautama objects, and the dispute over whether the king or Indra is supreme is settled by Sanatkumara in the king's favour. Pleased with the verdict, Vainya gives Atri a huge gift, which Atri shares with his sons before going to the forest.

scenes.B03C184S01: Atri seeks wealth from King Vainya, a quarrel with Gautama over the king's status is settled by Sanatkumara in the king's favour, and Atri receives great gifts.

shots.B03C184S01H01: Markandeya tells how the sage Atri, wanting wealth before retiring to the forest, is urged by his wife to seek gifts from King Vainya.
shots.B03C184S01H02: Atri praises Vainya at the sacrifice, and Gautama angrily replies that Indra alone is the highest sovereign.
shots.B03C184S01H03: The sages' quarrel draws attention at the sacrifice, and Kasyapa asks the disputants what the matter is.
shots.B03C184S01H04: The Munis take the question to Sanatkumara, who rules that the king is the protector and lord of men's destinies.
shots.B03C184S01H05: Vainya, pleased with the verdict, gives Atri a hundred million gold coins and ten bharas of gold, which Atri shares with his sons before going to the forest.

B03C185.summary: Markandeya says the goddess Saraswati once answered Tarkshya's questions about how a man can keep to virtue. She describes the rewards of Vedic study and of gifts, including cows, bullocks, clothes, gold and daughters in marriage, and of offerings to the sacred fire. Tarkshya then asks her for the rules for keeping the sacred fire.

scenes.B03C185S01: Saraswati, asked by Tarkshya about virtue, lists the rewards of study, gifts and offerings, and Tarkshya asks for the rules for keeping the sacred fire.

shots.B03C185S01H01: Markandeya says Saraswati once answered Tarkshya's question about how a man can keep to virtue and what he should offer.
shots.B03C185S01H02: Markandeya notes that Tarkshya was eager to learn, and Saraswati begins to answer.
shots.B03C185S01H03: Saraswati says that Vedic study leads to heaven, then lists the rewards for gifts of cows, bullocks, clothes, gold and daughters, and for steady offerings to the fire.
shots.B03C185S01H04: Tarkshya asks Saraswati for the rules for keeping the sacred fire as set out in the Vedas.

B03C186.summary: Yudhishthira asks Markandeya for the story of Vaivasvata Manu. Manu, while doing penance, rescues a small fish, which grows until he takes it to the sea, and the fish warns him of a coming flood and tells him to build a boat and gather the seeds. The fish tows the boat to the Himalaya and reveals itself as Brahma, who will recreate the world through Manu. Markandeya says that hearing this story brings merit and heaven.

scenes.B03C186S01: Manu rescues a fish, is warned of a flood, survives in a boat tied to a horned fish, and is told that Brahma will recreate the world through him.

shots.B03C186S01H01: Yudhishthira asks Markandeya to tell the history of Vaivasvata Manu.
shots.B03C186S01H02: Manu rescues a fish that grows until he takes it to the sea; the fish warns of a flood, guides Manu's boat to the Himalaya, and reveals itself as Brahma, who will recreate the world.
shots.B03C186S01H03: Markandeya says that Manu recreated the world after the flood and that hearing this story brings merit and heaven.

B03C187.summary: Yudhishthira asks Markandeya, who has lived through many ages, to explain the causes of things. Markandeya praises the Lord who creates the world, describes the lengths of the four yugas and the decline of the Kali age, and then tells how the world is destroyed by drought, seven suns, a fire, and floods. Alone on the waters, he finds the boy-god resting on a banyan leaf, enters his body, sees the whole universe within him, and asks him to explain it.

scenes.B03C187S01: Yudhishthira asks Markandeya to explain the causes of things; Markandeya describes the yugas, the destruction of the world, and his vision of the boy-god who holds the universe.

shots.B03C187S01H01: Yudhishthira, honouring Markandeya's long life, asks him to explain the causes of things and praises his knowledge of creation.
shots.B03C187S01H02: Markandeya praises the Lord who creates all things, gives the lengths of the four yugas and a day of Brahma, and describes the decline of the Kali age into disorder, falsehood and corrupt rule.
shots.B03C187S01H03: Markandeya describes the end of the world: drought, seven suns drying up the waters, the fire Samvartaka, and years of rain and flood.
shots.B03C187S01H04: Alone on the waters, Markandeya finds a boy resting on a banyan leaf, enters his body, sees the whole universe inside him, and asks him to explain it.

B03C188.summary: The boy-god reveals himself as Narayana, the source and destroyer of all things, who appears in many forms, takes human birth when virtue fails, and creates and withdraws the worlds. He explains that he showed Markandeya the universe within him to cure his melancholy, and that he will create again when Brahma wakes. Markandeya recognises him as Janardana, now Krishna of the Vrishnis, and the Pandavas bow to him and are consoled.

scenes.B03C188S01: Narayana reveals his identity and his power; Markandeya recognises Janardana, now Krishna, and the Pandavas bow down and are consoled.

shots.B03C188S01H01: The god reveals himself as Narayana, the source of all things and the Lord in many forms, and says he showed Markandeya the universe to cure his melancholy.
shots.B03C188S01H02: Markandeya says the god he saw is Janardana, now Krishna of the Vrishni race, and urges the Pandavas to seek his protection.
shots.B03C188S01H03: The Pandavas, with Draupadi and the twins, bow to Janardana, who consoles them with gentle words.

B03C189.summary: Yudhishthira asks Markandeya what will happen in the Kali age: how men will live and eat, and when the Krita age will return. Markandeya describes how virtue shrinks from age to age, and how in the Kali age people deceive one another, castes blur, rulers and Brahmanas fail in their duties, and portents and disorder spread. He ends by saying that after these terrible times creation begins anew, and a Brahmana named Kalki will be born to restore order.

scenes.B03C189S01: Yudhishthira asks what the Kali age will bring; Markandeya describes the decline of virtue, social disorder and omens, and the coming of Kalki, who restores order.

shots.B03C189S01H01: Vaisampayana says Yudhishthira once more asks Markandeya about the future course of government on earth.
shots.B03C189S01H02: Yudhishthira asks what will happen in the Kali age, how men will live and eat, and when the Krita age will return.
shots.B03C189S01H03: Markandeya describes how virtue shrinks in each age, and how in the Kali age people deceive one another, castes blur, rulers and Brahmanas fail, and portents and disorder spread.
shots.B03C189S01H04: Markandeya says that after these terrible times creation begins anew, and a Brahmana named Kalki will be born to restore order and destroy the Mlecchas.

B03C190.summary: Markandeya says that Kalki will destroy thieves and robbers, hold a great horse-sacrifice, and give the earth to the Brahmanas, and then virtue and sacrifice will return in the Krita age. He closes his teaching on the ages and advises Yudhishthira to be merciful, humble and devoted to his people, and never to humiliate a Brahmana. Yudhishthira promises to follow this counsel, and the listeners are filled with wonder.

scenes.B03C190S01: Markandeya describes Kalki's restoration of order and gives Yudhishthira his closing counsel on kingship, which Yudhishthira promises to follow.
scenes.B03C190S02: The Pandavas and their companions are filled with joy and wonder at Markandeya's teaching.

shots.B03C190S01H01: Markandeya says Kalki will destroy thieves and robbers, give the earth to the Brahmanas after a horse-sacrifice, and restore virtue in the Krita age.
shots.B03C190S01H02: Markandeya sums up the four ages, says he has told all he has seen, and urges Yudhishthira to fix his mind on virtue and never humiliate a Brahmana.
shots.B03C190S01H03: Yudhishthira asks how he should protect his subjects and keep to the duties of his order.
shots.B03C190S01H04: Markandeya advises him to be merciful, truthful, humble and devoted to his people, and to expiate his faults with charity.
shots.B03C190S01H05: Yudhishthira promises to follow the instructions, saying that he has no greed, lust, fear or pride.
shots.B03C190S02H01: The Pandavas, Krishna and the Brahmanas are filled with joy and wonder at Markandeya's teaching.

B03C191.summary: Markandeya tells how King Parikshit of Ayodhya married a maiden on the condition that he never show her water, and how she vanished into a tank. His son Sala seized the sage Vamadeva's Vami horses and refused to return them, and Vamadeva's Rakshasas killed him. When Vamadeva again demanded the horses from Sala's successor, Dala, a dispute over a poisoned arrow ended with Dala's son killed, until the queen's plea freed Dala from sin and the horses were returned.

scenes.B03C191S01: Markandeya tells of King Parikshit's marriage and the frog-king's revelation, then of Sala's theft of the Vami horses from Vamadeva and Sala's death at the hands of Rakshasas.
scenes.B03C191S02: Dala aims a poisoned arrow at Vamadeva, which kills his son instead, and after the queen's plea he returns the horses to the sage.

shots.B03C191S01H01: Janamejaya asks Vaisampayana to tell the greatness of Brahmanas as Markandeya taught it.
shots.B03C191S01H02: Vaisampayana says that Yudhishthira asked Markandeya for the greatness of Brahmanas, and Markandeya begins with King Parikshit.
shots.B03C191S01H03: King Parikshit marries a maiden who vanishes into a tank, the frog-king reveals that she is his daughter, and Parikshit's son Sala later seizes Vamadeva's horses.
shots.B03C191S01H04: Vamadeva sends a disciple to ask for the horses back, the king refuses, and Vamadeva warns that Rakshasas will punish him.
shots.B03C191S01H05: Four Rakshasas sent by Vamadeva kill Sala, Dala is set on the throne, and Vamadeva demands the horses from him.
shots.B03C191S02H01: Dala's poisoned arrow kills his son Senajita, his second arrow fails, and the queen's plea frees him from sin.
shots.B03C191S02H02: Vamadeva accepts the queen's plea, and Dala gives the Vami horses back to him with reverence.

B03C192.summary: Markandeya explains that the royal sage Vaka lived long because of his great asceticism, and then recounts Vaka's meeting with Indra, who asks about the sorrows of the immortal life. Vaka answers that loss of loved ones, dependence on others, and the sight of the undeserving prospering are the chief pains of such a life. Indra then asks about its joys, and Vaka praises a simple meal eaten at home and shared with guests and Brahmanas.

scenes.B03C192S01: Yudhishthira asks about Vaka's long life and his meeting with Indra; Indra visits Vaka and asks about the sorrows of the immortal, which Vaka describes.
scenes.B03C192S02: Indra asks about the joys of a deathless life, Vaka praises a simple, honest meal shared with guests, and Indra returns to heaven.

shots.B03C192S01H01: The Rishis and Brahmanas ask Markandeya how Vaka became so long-lived.
shots.B03C192S01H02: Markandeya says Vaka's great asceticism is the reason, and that nothing more need be asked.
shots.B03C192S01H03: Yudhishthira asks Markandeya to recount the meeting between Vaka and Indra.
shots.B03C192S01H04: Markandeya describes Indra's rule after the war with the Asuras, the prosperity of the world, and Indra's visit on his elephant Airavata to Vaka's hermitage.
shots.B03C192S01H05: Vaka answers Indra's question about the sorrows of the immortal, naming separation from loved ones, dependence on others, and the insult of the poor by the rich.
shots.B03C192S02H01: Indra asks Vaka to describe the joys of the deathless life.
shots.B03C192S02H02: Vaka praises a simple meal eaten at home, the merit of feeding guests and Brahmanas, and the purity of a Brahmana who has been fed.
shots.B03C192S02H03: After speaking with Vaka, Indra returns to heaven.

B03C193.summary: Markandeya tells how King Suhotra of the Kurus and King Sivi, son of Usinara, meet on the road and each refuses to yield the way, both claiming equal worth. Narada quotes verses saying that the wicked should be overcome by goodness and the mean by charity. Suhotra then honours Sivi, walks round him, and gives him the way.

scenes.B03C193S01: Suhotra and Sivi refuse to yield the road, Narada quotes verses on goodness and humility, and Suhotra gives way out of honour.

shots.B03C193S01H01: Markandeya tells how King Suhotra and King Sivi refuse to yield the road, Narada quotes verses on virtue, and Suhotra finally gives way out of honour.

B03C194.summary: Markandeya tells how King Yayati, son of Nahusha, is approached by a Brahmana asking for wealth for his teacher. Yayati says he never boasts of gifts, never listens to requests for things he cannot give, and never regrets a gift. He gives the Brahmana a thousand cows.

scenes.B03C194S01: Yayati, son of Nahusha, gives a thousand cows to a Brahmana who asked for them for his teacher, saying he never boasts of or regrets a gift.

shots.B03C194S01H01: Yayati, son of Nahusha, gives a thousand cows to a Brahmana who asked for them for his teacher, saying he never boasts of or regrets a gift.

B03C195.summary: Markandeya tells how King Seduka sends a Brahmana to King Vrishadarbha, who had vowed to give Brahmanas only gold and silver. When the Brahmana asks for a thousand steeds, Vrishadarbha strikes him with a whip, then makes amends by giving him the whole day's revenue, which is worth more than a thousand horses.

scenes.B03C195S01: Seduka sends a Brahmana to Vrishadarbha for steeds, the king whips him, and then gives him the whole day's revenue as amends.

shots.B03C195S01H01: Seduka sends a Brahmana to Vrishadarbha, who had vowed to give only gold and silver; when the Brahmana asks for steeds the king whips him, then makes amends with the day's full revenue.

B03C196.summary: Markandeya tells how the gods test King Sivi: Agni takes the form of a pigeon and Indra that of a hawk. The pigeon seeks Sivi's protection and the hawk demands it as food, and Sivi offers flesh cut from his own body in its place. When the pigeon still outweighs his flesh, Sivi climbs onto the scale himself, and the gods reveal themselves and promise him a son, Kapataroman.

scenes.B03C196S01: Agni, as a pigeon, flees to King Sivi, pursued by Indra as a hawk; Sivi cuts his own flesh to match the pigeon's weight, and the gods reveal themselves and promise him a son.

shots.B03C196S01H01: Agni, as a pigeon, flees to King Sivi, and Indra, as a hawk, demands it as his food; Sivi offers his own flesh until the gods reveal themselves and promise him a son.

B03C197.summary: At King Ashtaka's horse-sacrifice, several kings ask Narada which of them will fall from heaven first. He says Ashtaka will fall for boasting of his gifts, Pratardana for giving his horses with a bitter remark, and Vasumanas for praising a flowery car the king never gave him. Narada says he himself will fall, since he is not Sivi's equal; Sivi, tested by the god Vidhatri, was willing to kill and cook his own son for a Brahmana.

scenes.B03C197S01: Narada names the kings who will fall from heaven and the reasons, and says he himself will fall because he is not equal to Sivi, whose self-sacrifice was a test by Vidhatri.

shots.B03C197S01H01: At Ashtaka's horse-sacrifice, Narada names the king who will fall first and gives reasons for Ashtaka, Pratardana and Vasumanas.
shots.B03C197S01H02: Narada says he will fall himself, since he is not Sivi's equal, and tells how Sivi was willing to cook his son for a Brahmana who was the god Vidhatri in disguise.

B03C198.summary: Markandeya tells the Pandavas of the royal sage Indradyumna, who fell from heaven when his merit was spent and went looking for anyone who knew him. Markandeya sends him to the owl Pravarakarna, who points to the crane Nadijangha, and the crane points to the tortoise Akupara, who remembers Indradyumna's great sacrifices. A heavenly car then takes Indradyumna back, and an aerial voice says that only virtue lasts. Markandeya adds that Krishna once raised King Nriga from hell to heaven.

scenes.B03C198S01: Indradyumna, fallen from heaven, is passed from Markandeya to the owl, the crane and the tortoise, who recalls his sacrifices; a heavenly car takes him back, and Markandeya notes that Krishna once raised Nriga.

shots.B03C198S01H01: Fallen from heaven, Indradyumna is passed from Markandeya to the owl, the crane and the tortoise, and the tortoise recalls his sacrifices and gifts, and a heavenly car takes him back.
shots.B03C198S01H02: Indradyumna returns to heaven with an aerial voice's praise of virtue, and Markandeya says he has witnessed this as one who lives long.
shots.B03C198S01H03: The Pandavas praise Markandeya, who says Krishna once raised King Nriga from hell to heaven.

B03C199.summary: Yudhishthira asks when and how charity wins entry to Indra's heaven. Markandeya lists the kinds of life and gift that are futile, names the Brahmanas who deserve gifts, and calls food the greatest of gifts. He then describes the long, hard road to Yama's realm, where a traveller's past gifts decide his comfort, and closes with teachings on purity, the limits of outward austerity, and the greater merit of gifts made at sacred times.

scenes.B03C199S01: Yudhishthira asks about charity, Markandeya lists futile gifts and lives and names the deserving recipients, with food the greatest gift, and Yudhishthira asks about the road to Yama.
scenes.B03C199S02: Markandeya describes the road to Yama's realm and its rewards, then teaches on honouring Brahmanas, gifts of cows, purity, and the superiority of knowledge over outward austerity.
scenes.B03C199S03: Yudhishthira asks about meritorious charity, and Markandeya explains the times and seasons when gifts earn the greatest merit.

shots.B03C199S01H01: Yudhishthira asks when and in what stage of life charity wins entry to Indra's heaven.
shots.B03C199S01H02: Markandeya lists the futile kinds of life and of gifts, such as gifts to thieves, false teachers, and those who sell the Vedas.
shots.B03C199S01H03: Yudhishthira asks how Brahmanas who accept gifts can save both others and themselves.
shots.B03C199S01H04: Markandeya says Brahmanas save others through recitation, mantras and sacrifice, names who should and should not be fed, and calls food the greatest gift.
shots.B03C199S01H05: Yudhishthira asks how far Yama's realm lies from the world of men and how one crosses the distance.
shots.B03C199S02H01: Markandeya describes Yama's road, eighty-six thousand yojanas long, where a traveller's past gifts decide his comfort, and says honouring Brahmanas pleases the gods.
shots.B03C199S02H02: Yudhishthira asks Markandeya to keep speaking on virtue and morality.
shots.B03C199S02H03: Markandeya says that washing a Brahmana's feet, giving a cow at birth, and giving to the virtuous bring great merit, and that a Brahmana's weapon is his anger.
shots.B03C199S02H04: Yudhishthira asks what purification keeps a Brahmana always pure.
shots.B03C199S02H05: Markandeya names three kinds of purity, says penance without a pure heart is useless, and holds that knowledge alone brings final liberation.
shots.B03C199S03H01: Yudhishthira asks Markandeya about the rules of meritorious charity.
shots.B03C199S03H02: Markandeya lists the times, seasons and places when gifts earn the greatest merit, and says there is nothing higher than giving.
